belief: I don't belong in church because of my past.
origins: A history of addiction, divorce, abortion, prison, affairs, or years away from God can make a church building feel like a courtroom. We imagine that everyone has a spotless record and that our past would be unwelcome. Sometimes this is reinforced by real experiences of being whispered about.
teaches: Paul writes to the Corinthians, “And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.” The Pharisees grumbled, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them,” which was a compliment, not an insult. Jesus said of the woman who anointed His feet, “because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much.” Paul adds, “If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” Hebrews says, “Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence.” The church is where forgiven people gather, and your past is not your identity.
self_statements: People like me do not belong.
If they knew my past, they would ask me to leave.
I have been too far away for too long.
I will bring shame on the church.
I need to clean up first.
errors: Calling myself by my worst moments.
Predicting that I will be rejected.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that I do not belong.
Ignoring that Christ has forgiven me.
questions: What exactly in my past do I think disqualifies me?
Has God forgiven it, according to Scripture?
What would it mean to be washed and justified?
Who in the church might understand my story?
What would help me take one step toward a welcoming community?
truth: Christ has washed, sanctified, and justified me. My past is forgiven, and I am a new creation. I belong in the community of forgiven people, and I can look for a church that welcomes sinners as Jesus did.
hw_truths: I was washed, sanctified, and justified.
I can approach the throne of grace.
My past is not my identity.
log: Each week, record one moment of welcome or one truth about forgiveness.
actions: State what you think would happen if people knew your past.
Bring unresolved sin to God and receive forgiveness.
Look for one that talks openly about grace.
Share your story with a mature believer.
prayer: Lord, You welcome sinners. Wash me and give me courage to be among Your people. Let my past be a testimony of Your mercy and not a reason to stay away. Amen.
hw_questions: What in my past worries me?
What does God say about it?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I was washed and justified, so I belong.”
